name: Parsley and mint chewing

lead: Some people chew fresh parsley or mint leaves after meals to freshen breath, especially after garlic- or onion-heavy food. It is a cheap, food-based habit that needs no products.

The fresh herb flavour and chewing-induced saliva may cover odour briefly. Parsley is described on Wikipedia as being credited in cooking with neutralising garlic odours. Wikipedia's halitosis article reports that dietary approaches lack strong evidence and describes such remedies as short-term masking, and no clinical study of chewing these leaves for breath was found.

paras: People chew a few fresh leaves after eating, or garnish meals with parsley and eat it, often as a no-product alternative to mints. The effect, if any, is brief.
Low in food amounts; peppermint can aggravate reflux, and parsley seeds are not recommended in pregnancy.

angle.text: Chewing fresh parsley or mint is a folk habit for freshening breath, especially after garlic- or onion-heavy meals. Parsley is credited in cooking with neutralising garlic odors, and no trial has tested chewing the leaves for breath.

lead: Chewing fresh parsley or mint leaves is a folk method for freshening breath, often after garlic- or onion-heavy meals. Parsley is widely used as a garnish and is described on Wikipedia as being credited in cooking with neutralising garlic odours.[1]

Wikipedia's halitosis article reports that dietary approaches lack strong evidence and describes mints and similar remedies as short-term masking.[2] No clinical study of chewing parsley or mint leaves for breath was found.

paras: Curly-leaf parsley is commonly served as a garnish on dishes such as potatoes, fish and steak.[1] Peppermint and spearmint oils are common sources of mint flavour in confectionery.[3]

Wikipedia notes normal culinary amounts of parsley are considered safe, while parsley seeds contain apiole and very large amounts may have uterotonic effects, so pregnant women are advised to avoid excess.[1] Peppermint may relax the lower oesophageal sphincter and aggravate reflux.[3]
Leaf chewing is described in lifestyle discussions as a cheap, food-based alternative to gum or mints.

lore.intro: The practice is passed on as common-sense kitchen lore.

claims.claim: Chewing parsley or mint removes garlic breath
